clue.text: Cloud formation that looks decidedly fishy

definitions.text: Cloud formation that looks decidedly fishy

parts.words: Cloud formation that looks decidedly fishy
parts.note: a sky of rippled cloud patterned like the scales on a fish's back

explanation.surface: A suspicious-looking cloud, as if something odd is going on up there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishy' suggests something dubious; here it is literal, as the dappled cloud resembles the markings of a particular sea fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows of small cirrocumulus clouds are named for their likeness to the striped pattern on a common oily fish.

clue.text: Having to do with a fight? C

definitions.meaning: split as two words, one boxing contest

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a matter concerns a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, A BOUT, and it is a single round of combat.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition meaning concerning, and an article plus a word for a boxing match.

clue.text: Eager to set out — and most H enthusiastic?

parts.note: keen means eager

indicators.note: the letters of the word set are shaken out into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone raring to set off is surely the most eager of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns SET into EST, which follows KEEN. 'Eager' also looks like part of the definition, but it supplies only the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A superlative of the adjective describing someone full of zeal.

clue.text: I subsequently turn out to be in shopkeeping

indicators.note: to turn out here is to come out differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: later means subsequently

explanation.surface: Someone predicts they will end up working in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn out' rearranges I LATER. 'to be in' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling goods to the public in small quantities is the trade of a shop.

clue.text: Out of work waiters?

parts.note: not restaurant staff on the dole but idle people who hang about waiting

explanation.surface: Unemployed restaurant staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waiters' suggests table service; here it means people who simply wait around doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idlers who laze about are, in a sense, people passing time without work.

clue.text: Thicken soup for culinary C purposes

indicators.note: soup suggests something stirred and mixed, so the letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction to thicken a soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soup' looks like the thing being thickened; it is the anagram signal on THICKEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Used attributively, as in a garden or utensils meant for cooking, the room where food is prepared names that purpose.

clue.text: Tenuously held border constituencies

definitions.meaning: won by a slim majority and so at risk at the next election
read literally, electoral districts lying on the edge or margin

explanation.surface: Frontier districts barely kept under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' suggests a frontier; read literally, the second half describes districts on the margin, while the first gives the political sense of a slim majority.
explanation.definitionFit: In British elections, districts won by a small majority are described by the narrow edge of victory, and literally they are on the edge.

clue.text: Fauna that can do the turkey So trot in South America?

definitions.text: Fauna that can do the turkey So trot in South America?

parts.words: Fauna that can do the turkey So trot in South America?
parts.note: the turkey trot is a dance, but the creature meant is a turkey-like bird of the South American forests; the stray So is print debris

explanation.surface: Which animals can dance the turkey trot in Latin America?
explanation.walkthrough: The turkey trot is a ragtime dance; the clue means a large game bird related to turkeys that walks about in tropical American woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: A large crested game bird of Central and South American forests, related to the turkey.

clue.text: Delightful bonus for the hedonist?

parts.note: an extra treat, and the very thing a pleasure-seeker wants more of

explanation.surface: A lovely extra perk for a pleasure-seeker.
explanation.walkthrough: A hedonist lives for enjoyment, so an extra helping of it is the ideal bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra enjoyment on top of what was expected is an additional delight.

clue.text: Left in a unit cut off from all support?

indicators.note: in says the L goes inside A ONE

parts.note: one is a single unit

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in a military unit with no backup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb meaning abandoned, but it is L. 'in' puts L inside A ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without help from anyone means standing solitary and isolated.

clue.text: Wealth set aside for the benefit of others

definitions.text: Wealth set aside for the benefit of others

parts.words: Wealth set aside for the benefit of others
parts.note: money held and managed by trustees on behalf of beneficiaries

explanation.surface: A description of money reserved for other people.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets held by trustees for a beneficiary form a legal arrangement named after that confidence.

clue.text: A collection of night-gear

indicators.note: of here means made out of, so the answer is formed from the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A heap of pyjamas and nightgowns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' signals that the answer is made from the letters of NIGHT-GEAR rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembly of people or things brought together is a collection.

clue.text: Make a big effort to pull up

explanation.surface: Straining hard to haul something upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain mightily, and to lift or haul something heavy upward.

clue.text: A tune's involvement with a beak

indicators.note: involvement suggests things twisted together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A melody somehow connected with a magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beak' is British slang for a magistrate, which the surface leans on; here it is a literal beak or nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare zoological adjective for having a prominent nose or snout.

clue.text: Allow a penalty, maybe

definitions.meaning: a punitive measure such as a trade embargo

explanation.surface: Should a penalty be permitted?
explanation.walkthrough: The word carries two opposite senses: official approval and a punitive measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Both authorisation and a punitive measure share this contronym.

clue.text: Displaced person, ringing Ruskin by mistake, empties his glass

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so DP goes round the other letters

parts.note: DP is the abbreviation for displaced person, a refugee

indicators.note: by mistake means the letters of Ruskin come out wrongly ordered

explanation.surface: A refugee telephones the critic John Ruskin in error and then downs a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' suggests a phone call; it means encircling. RUSKIN rearranged ('by mistake') gives RINKSU, which goes between D and P.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing one's drink in full is the phrasal verb for draining a glass.

clue.text: Sort of wire that the government has phased out

definitions.text: Sort of wire that the government has phased out

parts.words: Sort of wire that the government has phased out
parts.note: a wire is an old word for a cabled message; the state Post Office service sending them was ended

explanation.surface: A kind of cable the authorities withdrew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wire' suggests metal cable; it is old slang for a cabled message, a service the British Post Office ended in 1982.
explanation.definitionFit: A message sent by telegraph was commonly called a wire.

clue.text: An epic pen somehow associated with gloom

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of pen and gloom come together in some new order

explanation.surface: A writer's pen tied to a dark mood produces a heroic narrative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges PEN with GLOOM; 'associated with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is an extended narrative verse work about heroic deeds.

clue.text: Lengthy discussion held by a 24 with the natives, perhaps

definitions.text: Lengthy discussion held by a 24 with the natives, perhaps

parts.words: Lengthy discussion held by a 24 with the natives, perhaps
parts.note: 24 is the answer to 24 across, a person from the continent of Europe; the word meant first such a parley between traders and local people

explanation.surface: A long talk between a European visitor and local people.
explanation.walkthrough: The word came from Portuguese and was used of conferences between European traders and West Africans; it now means long-winded talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A tedious prolonged conference or fuss, originally a parley with local inhabitants.

clue.text: Colour used up to a point by Dickens's illustrator

parts.note: brown is a colour
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A shade employed only partly by the man who drew pictures for Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: Hablot K. Browne, known as Phiz, illustrated many of Charles Dickens's novels. 'up to a point' tempts as meaning partly, but 'a point' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: Hablot Knight Browne, signing as Phiz, drew the original plates for The Pickwick Papers and other Dickens novels.

clue.text: Retort I put in the letter box in the Royal Exchange

indicators.note: this second in says I POST goes inside R and E

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for exchange
to post is to put mail in a letter box

explanation.surface: A sharp reply mailed from the Royal Exchange in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Exchange is a historic building in the City of London. 'in' puts I POST between R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick sharp reply, originally a counterthrust in fencing.

clue.text: Quickly put the balance in the Post Office

indicators.note: in says the remainder goes inside PO

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for Post Office
the rest is the balance or remainder

explanation.surface: An instruction to deposit leftover money at a post office promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balance' suggests money in an account; it means the remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking, and a conjuror's word, meaning at speed.

clue.text: Praise from those who will be in the next Olympics

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Acclaim coming from athletes who will compete at the next Games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters straddling 'next Olympics'.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud or glorify someone highly.

clue.text: Comparatively few Turks can claim to be this

definitions.text: Comparatively few Turks can claim to be this

parts.words: Comparatively few Turks can claim to be this
parts.note: most of Turkey lies in Asia, with only a small part west of the Bosporus

explanation.surface: A remark about Turkish identity.
explanation.walkthrough: Only Thrace, the small corner of Turkey around Istanbul, lies on the European side of the Bosporus.
explanation.definitionFit: People from the western continent; few Turks live in that part of their country.

clue.text: She can turn in a couple of at articles

indicators.note: in says the turned word sits inside the pair of articles

parts.note: two indefinite articles, a and a

indicators.note: turn says the word for the container is read backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A woman is able to spin within two newspaper pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb; it is TIN, turned to NIT and put between A and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so 'She' stands for it.

clue.text: Overtures composed for middle-age French laymen

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Orchestral overtures written for medieval French amateurs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks musical, matching 'Overtures', but it signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval poet-musicians of northern France composed lyric and epic verse, outside the clergy.

clue.text: A highball for a winter sportsman

definitions.meaning: a ball hit high into the air, especially in cricket
someone who glides down snowy slopes

explanation.surface: A cocktail for someone who spends the winter on the slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: A highball is a whisky-and-soda drink, which the surface uses; here it is a ball skied high in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball hit very high, and a person on snow slopes, share this spelling.

clue.text: Dizzy time to celebrate

parts.note: Dizzy was the nickname of Benjamin Disraeli; 19 April marks his death with his favourite flower

explanation.surface: A giddy festive occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dizzy' looks like giddy, but it is the nickname of the Victorian prime minister Benjamin Disraeli, commemorated each 19 April.
explanation.definitionFit: The anniversary of Disraeli's death, observed by Conservatives with yellow spring flowers.
